		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Market Area</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We are a community-oriented bank offering a variety of financial services to meet the needs of the communities we serve. &nbsp;We are headquartered in Muncie, Indiana and offer our financial services through 39 full service retail financial center offices in Allen, Delaware, Elkhart, Grant, Greene, Hamilton, Jackson, Johnson, Knox, Kosciusko, Lawrence, Monroe, Randolph, St. Joseph and Wabash counties in Indiana. MutualBank also has wealth management offices in Fishers and Crawfordsville, Indiana and a loan origination office in New Buffalo, Michigan. &nbsp;The Bank has a subsidiary, Summit Mortgage,&nbsp;Inc., that operates a mortgage banking firm in Fort Wayne, Indiana. &nbsp; In addition, we originate residential mortgage and commercial loans in the counties contiguous to those counties. &nbsp;We also originate indirect consumer loans throughout Indiana and contiguous states as described in &#x201C;Lending Activities&nbsp;- Other Consumer Lending.&#x201D;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The market areas where MutualBank operates in Indiana have historically experienced an unemployment rate that exceeded the federal and state unemployment rates, however in last three&nbsp;years the rate in our market areas was reduced to below the state and federal rates. &nbsp;At the end of 2018, the unemployment rate (not seasonally adjusted) was 3.7% at the federal level and 3.4% at the state level, compared to 3.9% and 3.1% at the end of 2017 at the federal and state level, respectively. &nbsp;Our footprint had an unemployment rate of 3.1% and 2.8% at&nbsp;year-end 2018 and 2017, respectively.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Competition</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We face strong competition from other banks, credit unions, mortgage bankers and finance companies in originating commercial, real estate and other loans and in attracting deposits. &nbsp;Our wealth management division faces strong competition from other banks, brokerage firms, financial advisers and trust companies. &nbsp;We attract deposits primarily through our financial center network. &nbsp;Competition for deposits comes principally from local banks and credit unions, but also comes from the availability of other investment opportunities, including mutual funds. &nbsp;We compete for deposits by offering superior service and a variety of deposit accounts at competitive rates. &nbsp;We also offer alternative investment products through a broker/dealer.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Lending Activities</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">General. &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">Our loans carry either a fixed- or an adjustable-rate of interest. &nbsp;At December&nbsp;31, 2018, our net loan portfolio totaled $1.5 billion, which constituted 72.3% of our total assets. &nbsp;Our net loan portfolio, excluding loans held for sale, increased by 27.0% in 2018, primarily due to the Universal acquisition in the first quarter of 2018 along with indirect consumer loan and commercial loan growth in 2018.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Aggregate credit exposures to borrowers of up to $1.0 million may be approved by certain individual commercial loan officers. &nbsp;Aggregate exposures in excess of $1.0 million, but not in excess of $3.0 million, may be approved by the combined authority of officers that have loan authority up to $1.0 million individually. &nbsp;Aggregate exposures between $2.0 million, but no more than $8.0 million, may be approved by a majority vote of the Loan Committee. &nbsp;All aggregate exposures in excess of $8.0 million must be approved by the Board of Directors. &nbsp;&nbsp;Commercial Banking Officers may advance additional credit exposure for a commercial loan relationship requiring Board approval up to the lesser of: 10% of the existing previously approved credit exposure to the client, or $100,000.&nbsp;Any additional exposure approved under the 10% Rule&nbsp;must be approved by the Senior Vice President of Commercial Banking, or his designee, and reported to the appropriate Loan Committee during the next meeting.</font>

As of December&nbsp;31, 2018, all loans within these relationships were performing as agreed.</font>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:7.95454545454545%;margin-right:7.95454545454545%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Consumer Closed End First Mortgages. &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">We originate loans secured by first mortgages on owner-occupied, one-to-four family residences in our market areas for purchase, refinance, home equity and construction purposes. &nbsp;At December&nbsp;31, 2018, these loans, including loans held for sale, totaled $468.5 million, or 31.2% of our gross loan portfolio.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We generally underwrite and document our one-to-four family loans based on the loan applicant&#x2019;s employment and credit history and the appraised value of the subject property, consistent with secondary market standards or other prudent underwriting guidelines. &nbsp;For loans with a loan-to-value ratio in excess of 80%, we generally require private mortgage insurance to reduce our exposure to 80%. &nbsp;Properties securing our one-to-four family loans are appraised or evaluated consistent with regulatory requirements and prudent lending principles. &nbsp;Origination and servicing practices include perfection of our lien position and appropriate monitoring of insurance and tax payments.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We generally underwrite and document our one-to-four family&nbsp;first lien position home equity loans based on the loan applicant&#x2019;s employment, credit history and the appraised value of the subject property, consistent with prudent underwriting guidelines. &nbsp;Nearly all first lien home equity loans have a maximum loan-to-value&nbsp;of 80% at origination. &nbsp;Properties securing our one-to-four family loans are appraised or evaluated consistent with regulatory requirements and prudent lending principles.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We originate consumer first mortgage one-to-four family loans on either a fixed- or adjustable-rate basis, and generally maintain a tax or insurance escrow account for these loans. &nbsp;Our pricing strategy for mortgage loans includes setting interest rates that are competitive with the secondary market and other local financial institutions and are consistent with our internal needs. &nbsp;Adjustable-rate mortgage or ARM loans are offered with initial fixed rate terms between one and 10&nbsp;years. After the initial period, the interest rate for each ARM loan adjusts annually for the remainder of the term of the loan using a margin over the standard one-year treasury index. &nbsp;During fiscal year 2018, we originated $10.8 million of one-to-four family ARM loans and $176.2 million of one-to-four family fixed-rate mortgage loans. &nbsp;By way of comparison, during fiscal year 2017, we originated $10.8 million of one-to-four family ARM loans and $176.4 million of one-to-four family fixed-rate mortgage loans.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Fixed-rate loans secured by one-to-four family residences have contractual maturities of up to 30&nbsp;years and are generally fully amortizing, with payments due&nbsp;monthly. &nbsp;A majority of loans with fixed-rate maturities in excess of 15&nbsp;years are sold on the secondary market. &nbsp;Some loans are retained if their terms meet current portfolio needs consistent with balance sheet objectives. &nbsp;These retained loans normally remain outstanding, however, for a substantially shorter period of time because of home sales, refinancing and other prepayments. &nbsp;A significant change in interest rates could alter considerably the average life of a residential loan in our portfolio. &nbsp;Our one-to-four family loans are generally not assumable, do not contain prepayment penalties and do not permit negative amortization of principal. &nbsp;Most are written using underwriting guidelines that make them readily saleable in the secondary market. &nbsp;At December&nbsp;31, 2018, our fixed-rate one-to-four family mortgage loan portfolio totaled $368.8 million, or 24.6% of our gross loan portfolio.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our one-to-four family residential ARM loans are fully amortizing loans with contractual maturities of up to 30&nbsp;years, with payments due&nbsp;monthly. &nbsp;Our ARM loans generally provide for specific minimum and maximum interest rates, with a lifetime cap and floor, and a periodic adjustment on the interest rate over the rate in effect on the date of origination. &nbsp;As a consequence of using caps, the interest rates on these loans may not be as rate sensitive as our cost of funds. &nbsp;In order to remain competitive in our market areas, we sometimes originate ARM loans at initial rates below the fully indexed rate. &nbsp;ARM loans generally pose different credit risks than fixed-rate loans, primarily because as interest rates rise, the borrower&#x2019;s required payments increase, which may increase the potential for default. &nbsp;Our payment history for ARM loans has not been substantially different from fixed rate loans. &nbsp;See &#x201C;Asset Quality&nbsp;- Non-performing Assets&#x201D; and &#x201C;Classified Assets.&#x201D;&nbsp;&nbsp;At December&nbsp;31, 2018, our one-to-four family ARM loan portfolio totaled $99.7 million, or 6.6% of our gross loan portfolio.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Construction-permanent loans on one-to-four family residential properties are obtained through referral business with builders, from walk-in customers and through referrals from realtors and architects. &nbsp;The applicant must submit complete plans, specifications and costs of the project to be constructed, which, along with an independent appraisal, are used to determine the value of the subject property. &nbsp;Loans are based on the lesser of the current appraised value and/or the cost of construction, including the land and the building. &nbsp;We generally conduct regular inspections of the construction project being financed. &nbsp;Residential construction loans are done with one closing for both the construction period and the long-term financing. Loans are generally granted with a construction period between six and 12&nbsp;months. During the construction phase, the borrower generally pays interest only on a&nbsp;monthly basis, and the loan is automatically converted to amortizing payments upon completion of the construction. &nbsp;Single family construction loans with loan-to-value ratios over 80% usually require private mortgage insurance.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Consumer Open End and Junior Liens. &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">At December&nbsp;31, 2018, our consumer loans on residential properties, including home equity lines of credit and subordinate home improvement loans, totaled $77.1 million, or 5.1% of our gross loan portfolio. &nbsp;Unused home equity lines of credit totaled $97.2 million at December&nbsp;31, 2018. These loans may be originated in amounts, together with the amount of the existing first mortgage, of up to 100% of the value of the property securing the loan. &nbsp;The term to maturity on our home equity and home improvement loans may be up to 15&nbsp;years. Most home equity lines of credit have a maximum term to maturity of 20&nbsp;years and require a minimum&nbsp;monthly payment based on the outstanding loan balance per&nbsp;month, which amount may be re-borrowed at any time during the first ten years. &nbsp;A limited number of home equity lines of credit are approved with&nbsp;monthly payments of accrued interest only. &nbsp;Other consumer loan terms vary according to the type of collateral, length of contract and creditworthiness of the borrower.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Commercial Real Estate Lending</font><font style="display:inline;">. &nbsp;We offer a variety of commercial real estate (&#x201C;CRE&#x201D;) loans for acquisition and renovation. &nbsp;These loans are secured by the real estate and improvements financed, and the collateral ranges from industrial and commercial buildings to churches, office buildings and multi-family housing complexes. &nbsp;We also have a limited amount of farm loans. &nbsp;At December&nbsp;31, 2018, commercial real estate loans, including multi-family, totaled $485.8 million, or 32.4% of our gross loan portfolio. During fiscal year 2018, we increased commercial real estate loan originations 59.4% to $75.3 million from $47.3 million in 2017.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our loans secured by commercial real estate are originated with either a fixed or adjustable interest rate. &nbsp;The interest rate on adjustable-rate loans is based on a variety of indices, generally determined through negotiation with the borrower. &nbsp;Loan-to-value ratios on our commercial real estate loans typically do not exceed 80% of the appraised value, as of origination, of the property securing the loan. &nbsp;These loans typically require&nbsp;monthly payments, are fully amortizing and generally have maximum amortizations of 20&nbsp;years. Loans with amortizations over 20&nbsp;years require a loan-to-value ratio of 75% or less.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Loans secured by commercial real estate are underwritten based on the income-producing potential of the property and the financial strength of the borrower. &nbsp;For income-producing properties, net operating income must be sufficient to cover the payments related to the outstanding debt. &nbsp;Owner-occupied CRE loans are underwritten based on the borrower&#x2019;s ability to generate cash flow sufficient to repay the loan. &nbsp;We may require personal guarantees of the borrowers in addition to the real estate as collateral for such loans. &nbsp;We also generally require an assignment of rents or leases in order to be assured that the cash flow from the real estate can be used to repay the debt. &nbsp;Appraisals on properties securing commercial real estate loans are performed by qualified independent appraisers approved by MutualBank&#x2019;s Board of Directors, consistent with regulatory requirements. &nbsp;See &#x201C;Loan Originations, Purchases, Sales and Repayments&#x201D; in this Item&nbsp;1. &nbsp;In order to monitor the adequacy of cash flows on CRE loans, the borrower is required to provide periodic financial information for loans in excess of $350,000.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Loans secured by commercial real estate are generally larger and involve a greater degree of credit risk than one-to-four family residential mortgage loans. &nbsp;Commercial real estate loans typically involve large balances to single borrowers or groups of related borrowers. &nbsp;Because payments on loans secured by commercial real </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;">estate are often dependent on the successful operation or management of the properties, repayment of such loans may be subject to adverse conditions in the real estate market or the economy. &nbsp;If the cash flow from the project is reduced, or if leases are not obtained or renewed, the borrower&#x2019;s ability to repay the loan may be impaired. &nbsp;See &#x201C;Asset Quality&nbsp;- Non-performing Assets&#x201D; in this Item&nbsp;1.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Construction and Development Lending</font><font style="display:inline;">. &nbsp;MutualBank makes a variety of commercial loans for the purpose of construction or development of commercial real estate.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Existing residential development loans are typically provided on property located within our market areas and are granted to developers and builders with previous borrowing experience with MutualBank. &nbsp;Financing of a development may include funding of land acquisition and development costs for lots as well as individual construction loans for speculative or pre-sold homes. &nbsp;New activity in residential development and construction lending has been limited by economic conditions for the past several&nbsp;years. We also provide construction-permanent financing for owner-occupied commercial properties for our business customers in our market areas as well as some income-producing property to established borrowers. &nbsp;We have a limited number of commercial real estate development loans. &nbsp;At December&nbsp;31, 2018, we had $53.3 million in construction and development loans outstanding, representing 3.6% of our gross loan portfolio.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Loans financing land development may include funding the acquisition of the land, the infrastructure and lot sales. &nbsp;Development loans are secured by real estate and repaid through proceeds from the sale of lots. &nbsp;The maximum loan amount should not exceed 75% of the appraised value and projected lot sales should show full payout within 24&#8209;36&nbsp;months of each phase being financed. &nbsp;Where the development loan is to be repaid through lot sales to third parties, the loan should be paid in full when no more than 80% of the lots in the phase or development are sold. Release payments should not be less than 85% of the net sales proceeds, or 125% of the original committed amount per lot, whichever is greater.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Construction financing must be supported by prints and specs, and an appraisal by an approved appraiser. &nbsp;Construction draws must be supported by a detailed list of work completed, and where appropriate, lien waivers from all contractors. &nbsp;All construction loans should have a maturity date with a written end financing commitment. We also provide end financing to qualified borrowers. &nbsp;Our maximum advance on residential pre-sold and owner occupied commercial loans is 80% of appraised value.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Because of the uncertainties inherent in estimating construction and development costs and the market for the project upon completion, there is risk inherent in the accuracy of estimated total loan funds required to complete a project, the related loan-to-value ratios and the likelihood of ultimate success of the project. &nbsp;These loans also involve many of the same risks discussed above regarding commercial real estate loans and tend to be more sensitive to general economic conditions than many other types of loans. &nbsp;Economic conditions in our market could cause borrowers to be unable to repay development loans due to reduced ability to market the properties consistent with original pro-forma estimates. &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Other Consumer Lending</font><font style="display:inline;">. &nbsp;Consumer loans, other than those secured by real estate, generally have shorter terms to maturity and carry higher rates of interest than residential mortgage loans. &nbsp;This reduces our exposure to interest rate risk on these loans. In addition, consumer loan products help to expand and create stronger ties to our customer base by increasing the number of customer relationships and providing cross-marketing opportunities. &nbsp;We offer a variety of secured consumer loans, including auto, boat and recreational vehicle loans, and loans secured by savings deposits. &nbsp;We also offer credit cards and unsecured consumer loans. &nbsp;We originate consumer loans both in our market area through our financial centers and throughout Indiana as well as making consumer loans to customers residing in contiguous states through our indirect lending program. &nbsp;We employ credit scoring models for these types of consumer loan applications. &nbsp;These models evaluate credit and application attributes, with a review of the borrower&#x2019;s employment and credit history and an assessment of the borrower&#x2019;s ability to repay the loan. &nbsp;Consumer loans may entail greater risk than one-to-four family residential mortgage loans, especially consumer loans secured by rapidly depreciable assets, such as automobiles, boats and recreational vehicles. &nbsp;In these cases, any repossessed collateral for a defaulted loan may not provide an adequate source of repayment of the outstanding loan balance. &nbsp;As a </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">12</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#TOC"><font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;">result, consumer loan collections are dependent on the borrower&#x2019;s continuing financial stability and, thus, are more likely to be adversely affected by economic downturn, job loss, divorce, illness or personal bankruptcy. &nbsp;At December&nbsp;31, 2018, our consumer loan portfolio, excluding real estate secured loans, totaled $267.2 million, or 17.8% of our gross loan portfolio.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">At December&nbsp;31, 2018, auto loans totaled $43.7 million, or 2.9% of our gross loan portfolio. &nbsp;Auto loans may be written for up to six&nbsp;years and usually have a fixed rate of interest. &nbsp;Loan-to-value ratios are up to 100% of the MSRP or 120% of invoice for new autos and 110% of value on used cars, based on valuation from official used car guides. &nbsp;Loans for boats and recreational vehicles totaled $216.6 million at December&nbsp;31, 2018, or 14.4% of our gross loan portfolio. &nbsp;Approximately $107.6 million of auto, boat and recreational vehicle loans&nbsp;originated&nbsp;during 2018&nbsp;were originated indirectly through dealers and retailers. &nbsp;At December 31,&nbsp;2018, auto, boat and recreational vehicle loans originated indirectly through dealers and retailers were $224.9 million compared to $162.4 at December 31, 2017, an increase of 38.5%. We generally buy indirect auto, boat and recreational vehicle loans on a rate basis, paying the dealer a cash payment for loans with an interest rate in excess of the rate we require. &nbsp;This premium is amortized over the remaining life of the loan. &nbsp;As specified in written agreements with these dealers, if a loan prepays or is&nbsp;charged-off within the first six months, the remaining premium is charged to future amounts owed to that dealer.&nbsp;If the dealer stops doing business with us, there is no longer a dealer reserve or other guarantee of payment required.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Commercial Business Lending</font><font style="display:inline;">. &nbsp;At December&nbsp;31, 2018, commercial business loans totaled $149.4 million, or 10.0% of our gross loan portfolio. &nbsp;Most of our commercial business loans have been extended to finance businesses in our market area. &nbsp;Credit accommodations extended include lines of credit for working capital needs, term loans to purchase capital goods and real estate, development lending to foster residential, business and community growth and agricultural lending for inventory and equipment financing.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our commercial business lending policy includes credit file documentation and analysis of the borrower&#x2019;s background, capacity to repay the loan, the adequacy of the borrower&#x2019;s capital and collateral as well as an evaluation of other conditions affecting the borrower. &nbsp;Analysis of the borrower&#x2019;s past, present and future cash flows also is an important aspect of our credit analysis. &nbsp;We may obtain personal guarantees on our commercial business loans. &nbsp;Nonetheless, these loans are believed to carry higher credit risk than residential loans. &nbsp;Unlike residential mortgage loans, commercial business loans are typically made on the basis of the borrower&#x2019;s ability to make repayment from the cash flow of the borrower&#x2019;s business. &nbsp;As a result, the availability of funds for the repayment of commercial business loans may substantially depend on the success of the business itself (which, in turn, often depends in part upon general economic conditions). &nbsp;Our commercial business loans are usually secured by business assets. &nbsp;However, the collateral securing the loans may depreciate over time, may be difficult to appraise and may fluctuate in value based on the success of the business.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The terms of loans extended on the security of machinery and equipment are based on the projected useful life of the machinery and equipment, generally not to exceed seven&nbsp;years. Lines of credit generally are available to borrowers for up to 12&nbsp;months and may be renewed by us after an annual review of current financial information.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We issue a few financial-based standby letters of credit which are offered at competitive rates and terms and are generally on a secured basis. &nbsp;We continue to expand our volume of commercial business loans.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Loan Originations, Purchases, Sales and Repayments</font><font style="display:inline;">. &nbsp;We originate loans through referrals from real estate brokers and builders, our marketing efforts, our existing and walk-in customers, and through our subsidiary, Summit Mortgage,&nbsp;Inc. Historically, we have originated many of our non-real estate consumer loans through relationships with dealerships in Indiana. &nbsp;While we originate adjustable-rate and fixed-rate loans, our ability to originate loans depends upon customer demand for loans in our market areas. &nbsp;Demand is affected by local competition, interest rate environment and general market conditions. &nbsp;During the last several&nbsp;years, due to low market rates of interest, our dollar volume of fixed-rate, one-to-four family loans has exceeded the dollar volume of the same type of adjustable-rate loans. &nbsp;As part of our interest rate risk </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">13</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#TOC"><font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;">management efforts, we typically sell our fixed rate, one-to-four family residential loans, with terms equal to or greater than 15&nbsp;years, on the secondary market. &nbsp;In periods of economic uncertainty, the ability of financial institutions, including us, to originate or purchase large dollar volumes of loans may be substantially reduced or restricted, with a resultant decrease in interest income.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company originates consumer loans, other than loans secured by real estate, in Indiana and contiguous states through our indirect lending program. &nbsp;The indirect lending consumer portfolio consists of loans for autos, boats and recreational vehicles.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">During the&nbsp;year ended December&nbsp;31, 2018, we sold $122.3 million of one-to-four family mortgage loans on the secondary market to Freddie Mac (&#x201C;FHLMC&#x201D;), Federal Home Loan Bank of Indianapolis (&#x201C;FHLBI&#x201D;) and other investors. &nbsp;As part of our interest rate risk management, the Company chose to sell these loans and recognized a gain on sale of $3.1 million. &nbsp;Servicing was retained on all loans originated through MutualBank but not through our subsidiary, Summit Mortgage.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Asset Quality</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Collection Procedures. &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">When a borrower fails to make a payment on a mortgage loan on or before the default date, a late charge and delinquency notice is mailed. &nbsp;All delinquent accounts are reviewed by a loss mitigation counselor, who attempts to cure the delinquency by contacting the borrower once the loan is 30&nbsp;days past due. &nbsp;If the loan becomes 30&nbsp;days delinquent, the loss mitigation counselor will generally contact the borrower by phone or send a letter to the borrower in order to identify the reason for the delinquency. &nbsp;Once the loan becomes 60&nbsp;days delinquent, the borrower is asked to pay the delinquent amount in full or establish an acceptable repayment plan to bring the loan current. &nbsp;Prior to foreclosure, a drive-by inspection is made to determine the condition of the property. &nbsp;If the account becomes 120&nbsp;days delinquent, and an acceptable repayment plan has not been agreed upon, a collection officer will generally refer the account to </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">15</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#TOC"><font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;">legal counsel, with instructions to prepare a notice of intent to foreclose. &nbsp;The notice of intent to foreclose allows the borrower up to 30&nbsp;days to bring the account current. &nbsp;During this 30&#8209;day period, the loss mitigation counselor may accept a repayment plan from the borrower that would bring the account current prior to foreclosure.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">For consumer loans, a similar collection process is followed, with the initial written contact being made once the loan is 20&nbsp;days past due.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Commercial loan relationships exceeding $350,000 are reviewed on a regular basis by the commercial credit department. &nbsp;Larger relationships are monitored through a system of internal and external loan review. &nbsp;All relationships that are deemed to warrant special attention are monitored at least quarterly. &nbsp;Individual commercial officers maintain communication with borrowers and recommend action plans to a Loan Quality Review committee which meets&nbsp;monthly to discuss credits graded Special Mention or worse. &nbsp;The Asset Classification committee meets quarterly and establishes specific allocations, based on appraisals or discounted cash flow analysis, for relationships that are deemed to be under-collateralized and at risk of non-payment. &nbsp;Collection and loss mitigation efforts are a cooperative effort between the Commercial Loan Department and the Risk Management Division.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Non-performing Assets. &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">The table below sets forth the amounts and categories of non-performing assets at the dates indicated. &nbsp;Generally, loans are placed on non-accrual status when the loan becomes more than 90&nbsp;days delinquent or sooner when collection of interest becomes doubtful. &nbsp;At December&nbsp;31, 2018, we had troubled debt restructurings totaling $3.3 million, $694,000 of which were included in non-accruing loans. &nbsp;Troubled debt restructurings involve forgiving a portion of interest or principal or making other adjustments to assist a borrower who is unable to meet the original terms of the loan. &nbsp;These restructurings are included in non-accruing loans until they perform according to the modified terms for six&nbsp;months. Then, if continued payments under the modified terms are deemed probable, and it is anticipated all principal will be recovered, they are removed from non-accrual status. &nbsp;Foreclosed assets include assets acquired in settlement of loans.</font>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#TOC"><font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Classified Assets. &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">Our regulators require that we classify loans and other assets, such as debt and equity securities considered to be of lesser quality, as &#x201C;substandard,&#x201D; &#x201C;doubtful&#x201D; or &#x201C;loss.&#x201D;&nbsp;&nbsp;An asset is considered &#x201C;substandard&#x201D; if it is inadequately protected by the current net worth and paying capacity of the obligor or of the collateral pledged, if any. &nbsp;&#x201C;Substandard&#x201D; assets include those characterized by the &#x201C;distinct possibility&#x201D; that the insured institution will sustain &#x201C;some loss&#x201D; if the deficiencies are not corrected. &nbsp;Assets classified as &#x201C;doubtful&#x201D; have all of the weaknesses inherent in those classified &#x201C;substandard,&#x201D; with the added characteristic that the weaknesses present make &#x201C;collection or liquidation in full,&#x201D; on the basis of currently existing facts, conditions, and values, &#x201C;highly questionable and improbable.&#x201D;&nbsp;&nbsp;Assets classified as &#x201C;loss&#x201D; are those considered &#x201C;uncollectible&#x201D; and of such little value that their continuance as assets without the establishment of a specific loss reserve is not warranted.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">When an insured institution classifies problem assets as either substandard or doubtful, it may establish general allowances for loan losses in an amount deemed prudent by management and approved by the board of directors. &nbsp;General allowances represent loss allowances that have been established to recognize the inherent risk associated with lending activities, but which, unlike specific allowances, have not been allocated to particular problem assets. &nbsp;When an insured institution classifies problem assets as &#x201C;loss,&#x201D; it is required either to establish a specific allowance for losses equal to 100% of that portion of the asset so classified or to charge off such amount. &nbsp;Our determination as to the classification of our assets and the amount of our valuation allowances is subject to review by our regulators, which may order the establishment of additional general or specific loss allowances.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In connection with the filing of the Bank&#x2019;s periodic reports in accordance with our classification of assets policy, we regularly review the problem assets in our portfolio to determine whether any assets require classification in accordance with applicable regulations. &nbsp;On the basis of management&#x2019;s review, at December&nbsp;31, 2018, we had classified $22.6 million of the Bank&#x2019;s assets as substandard or doubtful; $2.0 million in other real estate owned and repossessed assets and $20.6 million in substandard loans. &nbsp;The total amount classified represented 11.2% of our stockholders&#x2019; equity and 1.1% of our assets at December&nbsp;31, 2018, compared to 11.5% and 1.1%, respectively, at December&nbsp;31, 2017. &nbsp;See Note&nbsp;6 of the Notes&nbsp;to Consolidated Financial Statements in Item&nbsp;8 of this Form&nbsp;10&#8209;K for additional information about our classified assets and credit risk profile of our loan portfolio.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Provision for Loan Losses</font><font style="display:inline;">. &nbsp;We recorded a provision for loan losses during the&nbsp;year ended December&nbsp;31, 2018 of $2.1 million, compared to $1.2 million for the&nbsp;year ended December&nbsp;31, 2017 and $850,000 for the&nbsp;year ended December&nbsp;31, 2016. &nbsp;The provision for loan losses increased in 2018 primarily due to an increase in the loan portfolio of $137.7 million&nbsp;or 11.8% over the last&nbsp;year, excluding loans held for sale and $177.2 million acquired loans from the Universal acquisition &nbsp;as of December 31, 2018. &nbsp;The loan mix has contributed to the increase in provision with commercial and non-real estate consumer loans making up 63.8% of the loan portfolio at the end of 2018 compared to 57.0% as of the end of 2017. &nbsp;Net charge-offs for both 2018&nbsp;and 2017 equaled $1.2 million, or 0.09% of total average loans in 2018 compared to 0.10% of total average loans in 2017. &nbsp;The provision for loan losses is charged to income to bring our allowance for loan losses to a level deemed appropriate by management based on the factors discussed below under &#x201C;Allowance for Loan Losses.&#x201D;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Allowance for Loan Losses</font><font style="display:inline;">. &nbsp;We maintain an allowance for loan losses to absorb losses inherent in the loan portfolio. &nbsp;The allowance is based on ongoing, quarterly assessments of the estimated losses inherent in the loan portfolio. &nbsp;Our methodology for assessing the appropriateness of the allowance consists of several key elements, including the general allowance and specific allowances for identified problem loans and portfolio segments. &nbsp;In addition, the allowance incorporates the results of measuring impaired loans as provided in FASB ASC 310,</font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;"> Receivables</font><font style="display:inline;">. &nbsp;These accounting standards prescribe the measurement methods, income recognition and disclosures related to impaired loans. &nbsp;See Note&nbsp;6 of the Notes&nbsp;to Consolidated Financial Statements contained in Item&nbsp;8 of this Form&nbsp;10&#8209;K.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The general allowance is calculated by applying loss factors to outstanding loans based on the internal risk evaluation of such loans or pools of loans. &nbsp;Changes in risk evaluations of both performing and nonperforming </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">18</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#TOC"><font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;">loans affect the amount of the general allowance. &nbsp;Loss factors are based on our historical loss experience as well as on significant factors that, in management&#x2019;s judgment, affect the collectability of the portfolio as of the evaluation date.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The appropriateness of the allowance is reviewed by management based upon its evaluation of then-existing economic and business conditions affecting our key lending areas and other conditions, such as credit quality trends (including trends in non-performing loans expected to result from existing conditions), collateral values, loan volumes and concentrations, specific industry conditions within portfolio segments and recent loss experience in particular segments of the portfolio that existed as of the balance sheet date and the impact that such conditions were believed to have had on the collectability of the loan. &nbsp;Senior management reviews these conditions quarterly in discussions with our senior credit officers. &nbsp;To the extent that any of these conditions is evidenced by a specifically identifiable problem credit or portfolio segment as of the evaluation date, management&#x2019;s estimate of the effect of such condition may be reflected as a specific allowance applicable to such credit or portfolio segment. &nbsp;Where any of these conditions is not evidenced by a specifically identifiable problem credit or portfolio segment as of the evaluation date, management&#x2019;s evaluation of the loss related to this condition is reflected in the general allowance for loan losses. &nbsp;The evaluation of the inherent loss with respect to these conditions is subject to a higher degree of uncertainty because they are not identified with specific problem credits or portfolio segments.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The allowance for loan losses is based on estimates of losses inherent in the loan portfolio. Actual losses can vary significantly from the estimated amounts. &nbsp;Our methodology, as described, permits adjustments to any loss factor used in the computation of the general allowance in the event that, in management&#x2019;s judgment, significant factors which affect the collectability of the portfolio as of the evaluation date are not reflected in the loss factors. &nbsp;By assessing the probable incurred losses inherent in the loan portfolio on a quarterly basis, we are able to adjust specific and inherent loss estimates based upon any more recent information that has become available. &nbsp;Although the economy is stabilizing in the communities we serve and unemployment rates have improved compared to recent&nbsp;years, management has concluded that our allowance for loan losses should be greater than historical loss experience and specifically identified losses might otherwise indicate. &nbsp;This is due to the increase in higher risk loans like consumer and commercial, as a&nbsp;percentage of total loans.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">At December&nbsp;31, 2018, our allowance for loan losses was $13.3 million, or 0.89% of the total loan portfolio, and approximately 145.9% of total non-performing loans. &nbsp;Our allowance for loan losses balance increased 7.2% from December&nbsp;31, 2017. Assessing the adequacy of the allowance for loan losses is inherently subjective as it requires making material estimates, including the amount and timing of future cash flows expected to be received on impaired loans that are susceptible to significant change. In the opinion of management, the allowance, when taken as a whole, is adequate to absorb reasonable estimated loan losses inherent in our loan portfolio.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">19</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:normal;">Investment Activities</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">MutualBank may invest in various types of liquid assets, including United States Treasury obligations, securities of various federal agencies, including callable agency securities, securities of state and political subdivisions, certain certificates of deposit of insured banks and savings institutions, certain bankers&#x2019; acceptances, repurchase agreements and federal funds. It also may invest in investment grade commercial paper and corporate debt securities and certain mutual funds.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Chief Financial Officer is responsible for the management of our investment portfolio, subject to the direction and guidance of the Asset and Liability Management Committee and the Board of Directors. &nbsp;The Chief Financial Officer considers various factors when making decisions, including the marketability, maturity and tax consequences of the proposed investment. &nbsp;The maturity structure of investments will be affected by various market conditions, including the current and anticipated slope of the yield curve, the level of interest rates, the trend of new deposit inflows, and the anticipated demand for funds via deposit withdrawals and loan originations and purchases.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The objectives of our investment portfolio are to provide liquidity when loan demand is high, to assist in maintaining earnings when loan demand is low and to maximize earnings while satisfactorily managing risk, including credit risk, reinvestment risk, liquidity risk and interest rate risk. &nbsp;See &#x201C;Item&nbsp;7A&nbsp;- Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk&#x201D;.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our investment securities currently consist of U.S. Agency securities, mortgage-backed securities, collateralized mortgage obligations, municipal securities and corporate obligations. &nbsp;Our mortgage-backed securities portfolio currently consists of securities issued under government-sponsored agency programs. &nbsp;See Note&nbsp;5 of the Notes&nbsp;to Consolidated Financial Statements contained in Item&nbsp;8 of this Form&nbsp;10&#8209;K.</font>
		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">While mortgage-backed securities carry a reduced credit risk as compared to whole loans, these securities remain subject to the risk that a fluctuating interest rate environment, along with other factors like the geographic distribution of the underlying mortgage loans, may alter the prepayment rate of the mortgage loans and affect both the prepayment speed and value of the securities.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Although the Bank has not had a trading portfolio in recent history, we are permitted by the Board of Directors to have a trading portfolio of up to $5.0 million and to trade up to $2.0 million in these securities at any one time. &nbsp;At December&nbsp;31, 2018, however, we did not have a trading portfolio. &nbsp;See Note&nbsp;5 of the Notes&nbsp;to Consolidated Financial Statements contained in Item&nbsp;8 of this Form&nbsp;10&#8209;K.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">A majority of MutualBank&#x2019;s investment portfolio is under the management of its wholly owned subsidiary, Mutual Federal Investment Company. &nbsp;Mutual Federal Investment Company, a Nevada corporation, holds, services, manages and invests that portion of the Bank&#x2019;s investment portfolio as may be transferred from time to time by the Bank to Mutual Federal Investment Company. &nbsp;Mutual Federal Investment Company&#x2019;s investment policy, for the most part, mirrors that of the Bank&#x2019;s. &nbsp;Mutual Federal Investment Company has hired a third-party investment advisor to manage its securities portfolio, subject to the oversight of its Board of Directors. &nbsp;At December&nbsp;31, 2018, &nbsp;the Company&nbsp;had $370.9 million in consolidated investment securities carried at fair value. &nbsp;The portfolio is comprised of available for sale securities. &nbsp;At that date, Mutual Federal Investment Company managed $355.7 million of the total available for sale portfolio.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The following table sets forth the composition of our investment and mortgage-related securities portfolio and our other investments at the dates indicated. The 2018 acquisition of Universal contributed to increases in our investment and mortgage-related securities portfolio and other investments. The acquisition accounted for an increase in investment securities available for sale of $87.8 million and Federal Home Loan Bank stock of $1.6 million. Details regarding the acquisition are discussed in Note 2 of these Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements contained in Item 8 of this Form 10-K.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;As of December&nbsp;31, 2018, our investment securities portfolio did not contain securities of any issuer with an aggregate book value in excess of 10% of our equity capital, excluding those issued by the United States Government, its agencies or government sponsored entities.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">MutualBank conducts periodic reviews to identify and evaluate each investment security to determine whether an other-than-temporary impairment (&#x201C;OTTI&#x201D;) has occurred. &nbsp;Economic models are used to determine whether an other-than-temporary impairment has occurred on these securities. &nbsp;While all securities are considered, the securities primarily impacted by other-than-temporary impairment testing are private-label mortgage-backed securities and trust preferred securities. &nbsp;During the&nbsp;years ended December&nbsp;31, 2018, 2017 and 2016 we did not recognize any OTTI on our investments. &nbsp;No securities in the portfolio were non-performing as of December&nbsp;31, 2018. &nbsp;The remaining trust preferred security&nbsp;was priced using a discounted cash flow analysis as of December&nbsp;31, 2018.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Bank&#x2019;s trust preferred security valuation was prepared by an independent third party. &nbsp;Their approach for </font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;">determining</font><font style="display:inline;"> fair value involved several steps including: (1)&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;">a detailed credit and structural evaluation of each piece of collateral in the trust preferred security; &nbsp;(2)&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">collateral performance projections for each piece of collateral in the trust preferred security; (3)&nbsp;terms of the trust preferred structure, as laid out in the indenture; and (4)&nbsp;discounted cash flow modeling.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">MutualFirst Financial uses market-based yield indicators as a baseline for determining appropriate discount rates, and then adjusts the resulting discount rates on the basis of its credit and structural analysis of specific trust preferred securities. &nbsp;The primary focus is on the returns a fixed income investor would require in order to allocate capital on a risk adjusted basis. &nbsp;There is currently little demand for pooled trust preferred securities; however, the Company looks principally to market yields for stand-alone trust preferred securities issued by banks, thrifts and insurance companies for which there is an active and liquid market. &nbsp;The next step is to make a series of adjustments to reflect the differences that exist between these products (both credit and structural) and, most importantly, to reflect idiosyncratic credit performance differences (both actual and projected) between these products and the underlying collateral in the specific trust preferred security. &nbsp;Importantly, as part of the analysis described above, MutualFirst considers the fact that structured instruments frequently exhibit leverage not present in stand-alone instruments,&nbsp;and makes adjustments as necessary to reflect this additional risk.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The default and recovery probabilities for each piece of collateral were formed based on the evaluation of the collateral credit and a review of historical industry default data and current/near-term operating conditions. &nbsp;For collateral that has already defaulted, the Company assumed no recovery. &nbsp;For collateral that was in deferral, the Company assumed a recovery of 10% of par for banks, thrifts or other depository institutions, and 15% of par for insurance companies. &nbsp;Although the Company conservatively assumed that the majority of the deferring collateral continues to defer and eventually defaults, we also recognize there is a possibility that some deferring collateral may become current at some point in the future.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;"></font>
		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:11.7647058823529%;margin-right:11.7647058823529%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:normal;">Sources of Funds</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">General. &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">Our sources of funds are deposits, borrowings, payment of principal and interest on loans, interest earned on or maturation of other investment securities and funds provided from operations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Deposits</font><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">We offer deposit accounts to consumers and businesses having a wide range of interest rates and terms. &nbsp;Our deposits consist of savings deposit accounts, NOW and demand accounts and certificates of deposit. &nbsp;We solicit deposits in our market areas as well as online through our internet banking product. &nbsp;The Bank participates in services through the Certificate of Deposit Account Registry Service (&#x201C;CDARS&#x201D;) and Insured Cash Sweep (&#x201C;ICS&#x201D;) deposit services. &nbsp;Reciprocal ICS and CDARs deposit accounts are no longer classified as brokered deposits as of 2018. &nbsp;The Bank both purchases CDARS and ICS deposits and participates in reciprocal CDARS and ICS deposit services for our customers. &nbsp;We primarily rely on competitive pricing policies, marketing and customer service to attract and retain these deposits. &nbsp;Occasionally we will accept brokered deposits from a deposit broker. &nbsp;At December&nbsp;31, 2018, our brokered deposits totaled $120.5 million, or 7.9% of total deposits, with an average interest rate of 2.29% and a 0.56&nbsp;year weighted-average maturity.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The flow of deposits is influenced significantly by general economic conditions, changes in money market and prevailing interest rates, and competition. &nbsp;The variety of our deposit accounts has allowed us to be competitive in obtaining funds and to respond to changes in consumer demand. &nbsp;We have become more susceptible to short-term fluctuations in deposit flows, as customers have continued to deposit in short-term products while rates remain low. &nbsp;We try to manage the pricing of our deposits in keeping with our asset/liability management, liquidity and profitability objectives, subject to competitive factors. &nbsp;Based on our experience, we believe that our deposits are relatively stable sources of funds. &nbsp;Our ability to attract and maintain these deposits and the rates paid on those deposits has been and will continue to be affected significantly by economic and market conditions.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The FRB requires all depository institutions to maintain non-interest bearing reserves at specified levels against their transaction accounts, primarily checking, NOW and Super NOW checking accounts. At December&nbsp;31, 2018, we were in compliance with these reserve requirements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The following table sets forth the dollar amount of deposits in the various types of deposit programs we offered at the dates indicated.&nbsp;The 2018 acquisition of Universal contributed to increases in our deposits, resulting in an increase in deposits of $315.2 million. Details regarding the acquisition are discussed in Note 2 of these Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements contained in Item 8 of this Form 10-K.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Borrowings</font><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">We also utilize borrowings as a source of funds, especially when they are less costly than deposits and can be invested at a positive interest rate spread, when we desire additional capacity to fund loan demand or when they meet our asset/liability management goals. &nbsp;Our borrowings historically have consisted of advances from the FHLBI. &nbsp;See Notes 14 and&nbsp;15 of the Notes&nbsp;to Consolidated Financial Statements contained in Item&nbsp;8 of this Form&nbsp;10&#8209;K.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We may obtain advances from the FHLBI upon the pledging of certain collateral. &nbsp;These advances may be made pursuant to several different credit programs, each of which has its own interest rate, range of maturities and call features. &nbsp;At December&nbsp;31, 2018 we had $292.5&nbsp;million in FHLB advances outstanding. &nbsp;Based on current collateral levels, we could borrow an additional $11.0 million from the FHLB at prevailing interest rates. Additional assets were available to collateralize if the need&nbsp;would have arisen. &nbsp;In order to have access to FHLB advances, we are required to own stock in the FHLBI. &nbsp;At December&nbsp;31, 2018, we had $13.0 million in FHLB&nbsp;stock.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We also are authorized to borrow from the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago&#x2019;s &#x201C;discount window.&#x201D;&nbsp;&nbsp;We have never borrowed from the Federal Reserve Bank and currently do not have any assets pledged to them for borrowing.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;">The Company acquired $5.0 million of subordinated debentures in the 2008 acquisition of another financial institution. &nbsp;The net balance of these securities as of December&nbsp;31, 2018 was $4.2 million due to the purchase accounting adjustment made at the time of the acquisition. &nbsp;The securities bear the prevailing three-month LIBOR rate plus 170 basis points. &nbsp;The Company has the right to redeem the trust preferred securities, in whole or in part, without penalty. &nbsp;These securities mature on September&nbsp;15, 2035.</font>

This term note bears a fixed rate of interest of 4.99% per annum and requires quarterly principal payments, which began March 31, 2018. The variable rate term note matures 5 years from the date of issuance, or February 28, 2023. This term note bears a rate of interest of the prevailing three-month LIBOR rate plus 195 basis points, which was 4.35% at December 31, 2018. The Company has the right to redeem either note at any time, in whole or in part, without penalty.</font>
