		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Strong competition within our market area may limit our growth and profitability.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Competition in the banking and financial services industry is intense. &nbsp;In our market area, we compete with commercial banks, savings institutions, mortgage banking firms, credit unions, finance companies, mutual funds, insurance companies and brokerage and investment banking firms operating locally and elsewhere. &nbsp;Many of these competitors have national name recognition, greater resources and lending limits than we do and may offer certain services or prices for services that we do not or cannot provide. &nbsp;Our profitability depends upon our continued ability to successfully compete in our market.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The financial services industry could become even more competitive as a result of new legislative, regulatory and technological changes and continued consolidation. &nbsp;Banks, securities firms and insurance companies can merge under the umbrella of a bank holding company, which can offer virtually any type of financial service, including banking, securities underwriting, insurance (both agency and underwriting) and merchant banking. Also, technology has lowered barriers to entry and made it possible for non-banks to offer products and services traditionally provided by banks, such as automatic transfer and automatic payment systems. &nbsp;Many of our competitors have fewer regulatory constraints and may have lower cost structures. &nbsp;Additionally, due to their size, many competitors may be able to achieve economies of scale and, as a result, may offer a broader range of products and services as well as better pricing for those products and services than we can.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">A tightening of credit markets and liquidity risk could impair our ability to fund operations and jeopardize our financial condition.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Liquidity is essential to our business. &nbsp;A tightening of the credit markets and the inability to obtain adequate funding to replace deposits and fund continued loan growth may affect asset growth, our earnings capability and capital levels negatively. &nbsp;We rely on a number of different sources in order to meet our potential liquidity demands. &nbsp;Our primary sources of liquidity are increases in deposit accounts, including brokered deposits, as well as cash flows from loan payments and our securities portfolio. &nbsp;Borrowings, especially from the FHLB and repurchase agreements, also provide us with a source of funds to meet liquidity demands. &nbsp;An inability to raise funds through deposits, borrowings, the sale of loans and other sources could have a substantial negative effect on our liquidity. &nbsp;Our access to funding sources in amounts adequate to finance our activities or on terms that are acceptable to us could be impaired by factors that affect us specifically, or the financial services industry or economy in general. &nbsp;Factors that could detrimentally impact our access to liquidity sources include adverse regulatory action against us or a decrease in the level of our business activity as a result of a downturn in the markets in which our loans are concentrated. &nbsp;Our ability to borrow also could be impaired by factors that are not specific to us, such as a disruption in the financial markets, negative views and expectations about the prospects for the financial services industry in light of the recent turmoil faced by banking organizations or continued deterioration in credit markets.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Goodwill and our core deposit premium could be deemed partially or fully impaired in the future, which would reduce our earnings and the values of our&nbsp;intangible assets.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">At December&nbsp;31, 2018, we had goodwill of $22.3 million and a core deposit premium of $3.6 million, due mainly to our 2018 acquisition of Universal. &nbsp;Under GAAP, we are required to periodically assess the value of these&nbsp;intangible assets based on a number of factors to determine if there is partial or full impairment. &nbsp;The factors taken into consideration include the market price of our stock, the net present value of our assets and liabilities and valuation information for similar financial institutions. &nbsp;This evaluation involves a substantial amount of judgment. &nbsp;If actual conditions underlying the factors differ from our assessment, the </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:11.7647058823529%;margin-right:11.7647058823529%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">40</font>

		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;">In response to the last financial crisis, Congress took actions that are intended to strengthen confidence and encourage liquidity in financial institutions, and the FDIC has taken actions to increase insurance coverage on deposit accounts. &nbsp;The Dodd-Frank Act created the CFPB.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">The CFPB has finalized a number of significant rules&nbsp;that could have a significant impact on our business and the financial services industry more generally. &nbsp;In particular, the CFPB has adopted rules&nbsp;impacting nearly every aspect of the lifecycle of a residential mortgage loan. &nbsp;The CFPB has also issued guidance which could significantly affect the automotive financing industry by subjecting indirect auto lenders, such as the Bank, to regulation as creditors under the Equal Credit Opportunity Act, which would make indirect auto lenders monitor and control certain credit policies and procedures undertaken by auto dealers.</font>

The FDIC and IDFI regulate the activities in which the Bank may engage primarily for the protection of depositors and not for the protection or benefit of stockholders. In addition, new laws and regulations may increase our costs of regulatory compliance and of doing business and otherwise affect our operations. New laws and regulations may significantly affect the markets in which we do business, the markets for and value of our loans and investments, the fees we can charge and our ongoing operations, costs and profitability. Regulatory changes regarding card interchange fee income do not currently apply to us but could change in the future. &nbsp;Further, legislative proposals limiting our rights as a creditor could result in credit losses or increased expense in pursuing our remedies as a creditor.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">The Dodd-Frank Act established 1.35% of total insured deposits as the minimum reserve ratio for the FDIC Deposit Insurance Fund effective September&nbsp;30, 2020. &nbsp;On September&nbsp;30, 2018, the Deposit Insurance Fund Reserve Ratio reached 1.36%. &nbsp;The FDIC must offset the requirement that the minimum reserve ratio reach 1.35% on institutions with assets less than $10 billion. &nbsp;To implement the offset requirement, FDIC regulations require that institutions with assets of $10 billion or more pay a surcharge during a temporary period and smaller institutions will receive credits whenever the reserve ratio reaches 1.38%. &nbsp;The FDIC notified the Bank of its individual credit amount in January 2019 and&nbsp;will apply credits each quarter that the reserve ratio is at least 1.38%, up to the full amount of a small bank&#x2019;s credit or assessment, whichever is less. &nbsp;In addition to the statutory minimum ratio, the FDIC must set a designated reserve ratio or DRR, which may exceed the statutory minimum. &nbsp;The FDIC has set 2.0% as the DRR.</font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our charter provides that any person or group who acquires beneficial ownership of our common stock in excess of 10% of the outstanding shares may not vote the excess shares. &nbsp;Accordingly, if you acquire beneficial ownership of more than 10% of the outstanding shares of our common stock, your voting rights with respect to the common stock will not be commensurate with your economic interest in the Company.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We rely on dividends from MutualBank for substantially all of the Company&#x2019;s revenue.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">MutualFirst&#x2019;s primary source of revenue is dividends from the Bank. &nbsp;In certain instances, the IDFI must be notified of dividends made from the Bank to the Company and may choose to limit Bank dividends. &nbsp;If the Bank is unable to pay dividends, MutualFirst may not be able to service its debt, pay its other obligations or pay dividends on the Company&#x2019;s common stock, which could have a material adverse impact on our financial condition or the value of your investment in our common stock.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our common stock trading volume may not provide adequate liquidity for investors.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our common stock is listed on the Nasdaq Global Market. &nbsp;However, the average daily trading volume in our common stock is less than that of many larger financial services companies. &nbsp;A public trading market having the desired depth, liquidity and orderliness depends on the presence of a sufficient number of willing buyers and sellers for our common stock at any given time. &nbsp;This presence is impacted by general economic and market conditions and investors&#x2019; views of our Company. &nbsp;Because our trading volume is limited, any significant sales of our shares could cause a decline in the price of our common stock.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our directors and executive officers have the ability to influence stockholder actions in a manner that may be adverse to the personal investment objectives of our stockholders.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2018, our directors and executive officers as a group beneficially owned 2,407,027 shares, or 27.4%, of our common stock (including immediately exercisable options for 172,142 shares). &nbsp;In addition, our employee stock ownership and 401(k)&nbsp;plan controlled 4.4% of our common stock on that date. &nbsp;Due to this significant collective ownership of or control over our common stock, our directors and executive officers may be able to influence the outcome of director elections or block significant transactions, such as a merger or acquisition, or any other matter that might otherwise be favored by other stockholders and could prevent any stockholder action requiring a supermajority vote under our articles of incorporation.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Item&nbsp;7.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management&#x2019;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operation<a name="Item7ManagementsDiscussionandAnalysisofF"></a></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Overview and Significant Events in 2018</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">MutualFirst is a Maryland corporation and a bank holding company headquartered in Muncie, Indiana, with operations in Allen, Delaware, Elkhart, Grant, Greene, Hamilton, Jackson, Johnson, Knox, Kosciusko, Lawrence, Monroe, Randolph, St. Joseph and Wabash counties in Indiana. &nbsp;It owns MutualBank, an Indiana commercial bank with 39 financial centers in Indiana, trust offices in Fishers and Crawfordsville, Indiana and a loan origination office in New Buffalo, Michigan. &nbsp;The Bank has a subsidiary, Summit Mortgage,&nbsp;Inc., that operates a mortgage banking firm in Fort Wayne, Indiana.&nbsp;MutualFirst also owns MutualFirst Risk Management, a captive insurance company based in Nevada and Mutual Risk Advisors, an information security consulting firm based in Indiana.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">MutualBank is an Indiana commercial bank subject to regulation, supervision and examination by the IDFI and the FDIC. &nbsp;MutualFirst is a bank holding company subject to examination, supervision and regulation by the FRB, which is subjected to regulatory capital requirements similar to those imposed on the Bank. &nbsp;For more details on these regulations see &#x201C;Item&nbsp;1. Business&nbsp;&#x2013; How We Are Regulated.&#x201D;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">At December&nbsp;31, 2018, we had $2.0 billion in assets, $1.5 billion in loans, $1.5 billion in deposits and $202.4 million in stockholders&#x2019; equity. &nbsp;On February 28, 2018, the Corporation acquired Universal, which resulted in $406.6 million of additional assets and the issuance of $42.3 million of common stock as partial consideration for the acquisition. &nbsp;The Bank&#x2019;s&nbsp;total risk-based capital ratio at December&nbsp;31, 2018&nbsp;was 13.0%, exceeding the 10.0% requirement for a well-capitalized institution. &nbsp;The ratio of average tangible common equity decreased to 8.72% as of&nbsp;year-end 2018 compared to 9.35% at&nbsp;year-end 2017. &nbsp;For the&nbsp;year ended December&nbsp;31, 2018, net income available to common shareholders was $18.9 million, or $2.25 per basic and $2.21 per diluted share, compared with net income available to common shareholders of $12.3 million, or $1.67&nbsp;per basic and $1.64&nbsp;per diluted share for 2017. &nbsp;Net income for 2018 includes $1.9 million of one-time merger and system conversion expenses, net of tax, related to the acquisition of Universal. The details of our 2018 performance are set forth below and in our Consolidated Audited Financial Statements contained in Item&nbsp;8 of this Form&nbsp;10&#8209;K, as well as&nbsp;details regarding the acquisition are discussed in Note 2.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Key aspects of our 2018 operations include:</font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">MutualWealth is the wealth management division of the Bank providing a variety of fee-based financial services, including trust, investment, insurance, broker advisory, retirement plan and private banking services, in the Bank&#x2019;s market area. MutualWealth produces non-interest income for the Bank that is tied primarily to the market value of the portfolios being managed. &nbsp;As of December&nbsp;31, 2018, MutualWealth had $495.0 million of fiduciary assets and generated $3.9 million in commission income during 2018.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">MutualFinancial Services is the brokerage division of the Bank providing a variety of fee-based financial services related to securities and investment transactions. MutualFinancial Services produces non-interest income for the Bank that is tied primarily to the volume of the transactions being processed. &nbsp;During 2018, MutualFinancial Services generated $812,000 in commission income.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our results of operations depend primarily on the level of our net interest income, which is the difference between interest income on interest-earning assets, such as loans, mortgage-backed securities and investment securities, and interest expense on interest-bearing liabilities, primarily deposits and borrowings. &nbsp;The structure of our interest-earning assets versus the structure of interest-bearing liabilities, along with the shape of the yield curve, has a direct impact on our net interest income. &nbsp;Historically, our interest-earning assets have been longer term in nature (i.e., fixed-rate mortgage loans) and interest-bearing liabilities have been shorter term (i.e., certificates of deposit, regular savings accounts, etc.). &nbsp;This structure would impact net interest income favorably in a decreasing rate environment, assuming a normally shaped yield curve, as the rates on interest-bearing liabilities would decrease more rapidly than rates on the interest-earning assets. &nbsp;Conversely, in an increasing rate environment, assuming a normally shaped yield curve, net interest income would be impacted unfavorably as rates on interest-earning assets would increase at a slower rate than rates on interest-bearing liabilities.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company continues to reduce the impact of interest rate changes on its net interest income by shortening the term of its interest-earning assets to better match the terms of our interest-bearing liabilities and by selling long-term fixed rate loans and increasing the term of certain liabilities. &nbsp;See &#x201C;Item&nbsp;7A&nbsp;- Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk&nbsp;- Asset and Liability Management and Market Risk&#x201D; in this Form&nbsp;10&#8209;K. &nbsp;It has been the Company&#x2019;s strategic objective to change the repricing structure of its interest-earning assets from longer term to shorter term to better match the structure of our interest-bearing liabilities and therefore reduce the impact interest rate changes have on our net interest income. &nbsp;Strategies employed to accomplish this objective have been to increase the originations of variable rate commercial loans and shorter term consumer loans and to sell longer term mortgage loans. &nbsp;The&nbsp;percentage of non-residential consumer and commercial loans to total loans has increased from 56.5% at the end of 2017 to 63.7% as of December&nbsp;31, 2018. &nbsp;We continued to see improvements in our markets during 2018&nbsp;and made significant progress toward achieving our strategic target loan mix through both organic non-residential consumer and commercial loan growth and the acquisition of Universal. &nbsp;On the liability side of the balance sheet, the Company is continuing to employ strategies intended to increase the balance of core deposit accounts, such as low cost checking and money market accounts. &nbsp;The&nbsp;percentage of core deposits to total deposits declined slightly from 69.1% in 2017 to 67.8% in 2018.&nbsp;These are ongoing strategies that are dependent on current market conditions and competition. &nbsp;The Company lengthens the term to maturity of FHLB advances when advantageous to lengthen repricing of the liability side of the balance sheet in order to reduce interest rate risk exposure.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">During 2018, in keeping with our strategic objective to reduce interest rate risk exposure, the Company also sold $122.3 million of long-term fixed rate loans, which reduced potential earning assets and therefore had a negative impact on net interest income. &nbsp;This was offset, in the short term, by recognizing a gain on the sale of these loans of $3.1 million.</font>
		</p>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Recent Accounting Standards</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">For discussion of recent accounting standards, please see Note&nbsp;3: Impact of Accounting Pronouncements to our Consolidated Financial Statements in Item&nbsp;8 of this Form&nbsp;10&#8209;K.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Critical Accounting Policies</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Notes&nbsp;to the Consolidated Financial Statements in Item&nbsp;8 of this Form&nbsp;10&#8209;K contain a summary of the Company&#x2019;s significant accounting policies. &nbsp;Certain of these policies are important to the portrayal of the Company&#x2019;s financial condition, since they require management to make difficult, complex or subjective judgments, some of which may relate to matters that are inherently uncertain. &nbsp;Management believes that its critical accounting policies include determining the allowance for loan losses, the valuation of foreclosed assets, mortgage servicing rights, valuation of intangible assets and securities, deferred tax asset and income tax accounting.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Allowance for Loan Losses</font><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">The allowance for loan losses is a significant estimate that can and does change based on management&#x2019;s assumptions about specific borrowers and current general economic and business conditions, among other factors. &nbsp;Management reviews the adequacy of the allowance for loan losses on at least a quarterly basis. &nbsp;The evaluation by management includes consideration of past loss experience, changes in the composition of the loan portfolio, the current condition and amount of loans outstanding, identified problem loans and the probability of collecting all amounts due.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The determination of the adequacy of the allowance for loan losses is based on estimates that are particularly susceptible to significant changes in the economic environment and market conditions. A worsening or protracted economic decline would increase the likelihood of additional losses due to credit and market risk and could create the need for additional loss reserves.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Foreclosed Assets</font><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">Foreclosed assets are carried at the lower of cost or fair value less estimated selling costs. &nbsp;Management estimates the fair value of the properties based on current appraisal information. &nbsp;Fair value estimates are particularly susceptible to significant changes in the economic environment, market conditions, and real estate market. &nbsp;A worsening or protracted economic decline would increase the likelihood of a decline in property values and could create the need to write down the properties through current operations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Mortgage Servicing Rights</font><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">MSRs associated with loans originated and sold, where servicing is retained, are capitalized and included in other assets in the consolidated balance sheet. &nbsp;The value of the capitalized servicing rights represents the fair value of the right to service loans in the portfolio. &nbsp;Critical accounting policies for MSRs relate to the initial valuation and subsequent impairment tests. &nbsp;The methodology used to determine the valuation of MSRs requires the development and use of a number of estimates, including anticipated principal amortization and prepayments of that principal balance. &nbsp;Events that may significantly affect the estimates used are changes in interest rates, mortgage loan prepayment speeds and the payment performance of the underlying loans. &nbsp;The carrying value of the MSRs is periodically reviewed for impairment based on a determination of fair value. &nbsp;For purposes of measuring impairment, the servicing rights are compared to a valuation prepared based on a discounted cash flow methodology, utilizing current prepayment speeds and discount rates. Impairment, if any, is recognized through a valuation allowance and is recorded as a reduction in loan servicing fee income.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:11.7647058823529%;margin-right:11.7647058823529%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">54</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:11.7647058823529%;margin-right:11.7647058823529%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:11.7647058823529%;margin-right:11.7647058823529%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#TOC"><font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:11.7647058823529%;margin-right:11.7647058823529%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Goodwill and Intangible Assets</font><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">MutualFirst periodically assesses the impairment of its goodwill and the recoverability of its core deposit intangible. &nbsp;Impairment is the condition that exists when the carrying amount exceeds its implied fair value. &nbsp;If actual external conditions and future operating results differ from MutualFirst&#x2019;s judgments, impairment and/or increased amortization charges may be necessary to reduce the carrying value of these assets to the appropriate value.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Goodwill is tested for impairment on an annual basis as of November&nbsp;30, or whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate the carrying amount of goodwill exceeds its implied fair value. &nbsp;No events or changes in circumstances have occurred since the annual impairment test that would suggest it was more likely than not goodwill impairment existed.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Securities</font><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">Under FASB Codification Topic 320 (ASC 320),</font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;"> Investments-Debt and Equity Securities</font><font style="display:inline;">, investment securities must be classified as held to maturity, available for sale or trading. &nbsp;Management determines the appropriate classification at the time of purchase. &nbsp;The classification of securities is significant since it directly impacts the accounting for unrealized gains and losses on securities. &nbsp;Debt securities are classified as held to maturity and carried at amortized cost when management has the positive intent and the Company has the ability to hold the securities to maturity. &nbsp;Securities not classified as held to maturity are classified as available for sale and are carried at fair value, with the unrealized holding gains and losses, net of tax, reported in other comprehensive income and do not affect earnings until realized.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The fair values of the Company&#x2019;s securities are generally determined by reference to quoted prices from reliable independent sources utilizing observable inputs. &nbsp;Certain of the Company&#x2019;s fair values of securities are determined using models whose significant value drivers or assumptions are unobservable and are significant to the fair value of the securities. &nbsp;These models are utilized when quoted prices are not available for certain securities or in markets where trading activity has slowed or ceased. &nbsp;When quoted prices are not available and are not provided by third party pricing services, management judgment is necessary to determine fair value. &nbsp;As such, fair value is determined using discounted cash flow analysis models, incorporating default rates, estimation of prepayment characteristics and implied volatilities.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company evaluates all securities on a quarterly basis, and more frequently when economic conditions warrant additional evaluations, for determining if OTTI exists pursuant to guidelines established in ASC 320. &nbsp;In evaluating the possible impairment of securities, consideration is given to the length of time and the extent to which the fair value has been less than cost, the financial condition and near-term prospects of the issuer, and the ability and intent of the Company to retain its investment in the issuer for a period of time sufficient to allow for any anticipated recovery in fair value. In analyzing an issuer&#x2019;s financial condition, the Company may consider whether the securities are issued by the federal government or its agencies or government sponsored agencies, whether downgrades by bond rating agencies have occurred, and the results of reviews of the issuer&#x2019;s financial condition.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">If management determines that an investment experienced an OTTI, management must then determine the amount of the OTTI to be recognized in earnings. &nbsp;If management does not intend to sell the security and it is more likely than not that the Company will not be required to sell the security before recovery of its amortized cost basis less any current period loss, the OTTI will be separated into the amount representing the credit loss and the amount related to all other factors. &nbsp;The amount of OTTI related to the credit loss is determined based on the present value of cash flows expected to be collected and is recognized in earnings. &nbsp;The amount of the OTTI related to other factors will be recognized in other comprehensive income, net of applicable taxes. &nbsp;The previous amortized cost basis less the OTTI recognized in earnings will become the new amortized cost basis of the investment. &nbsp;If management intends to sell the security or more likely than not will be required to sell the security before recovery of its amortized cost basis less any current period credit loss, the OTTI will be recognized in earnings equal to the entire difference between the investment&#x2019;s amortized cost basis and its fair value at the balance sheet </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:11.7647058823529%;margin-right:11.7647058823529%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">55</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:11.7647058823529%;margin-right:11.7647058823529%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:11.7647058823529%;margin-right:11.7647058823529%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#TOC"><font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:11.7647058823529%;margin-right:11.7647058823529%;"><p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;">date. &nbsp;Any recoveries related to the value of these securities are recorded as an unrealized gain (as accumulated other comprehensive income (loss) in stockholders&#x2019; equity) and not recognized in income until the security is ultimately sold.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company from time to time may dispose of an impaired security in response to asset/liability management decisions, future market movements, business plan changes, or if the net proceeds can be reinvested at a rate of return that is expected to recover the loss within a reasonable period of time.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Deferred Tax Asset</font><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">The Company has evaluated its deferred tax asset to determine if it is more likely than not that the asset will be utilized in the future. &nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s most recent evaluation has determined that, except for the amounts represented by the valuation allowance as discussed below, the Company will more likely than not be able to utilize the remaining deferred tax asset. The Company has generated average positive pre-tax pre-provision earnings of $19.1 million, or 1.2% of pre-tax pre-provision ROA over the previous five&nbsp;years. These earnings would be sufficient to utilize portions of the operating losses, tax credit carryforwards and temporary tax differences over the allowable periods. The analysis supports no additional valuation reserve is needed.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The valuation allowance established is the result of net operating losses for state franchise tax purposes totaling $35.0 million. &nbsp;See Note&nbsp;17 of the Notes&nbsp;to Consolidated Financial Statements contained in Item&nbsp;8 of this Form&nbsp;10&#8209;K.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Income Tax Accounting</font><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">We file a consolidated federal income tax return. &nbsp;The provision for income taxes is based upon income in our consolidated financial statements, rather than amounts reported on our income tax return. &nbsp;Deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized for future tax consequences attributable to differences between the financial statement carrying amounts of existing assets and liabilities and their respective tax bases. &nbsp;Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in the&nbsp;years in which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled. &nbsp;The effect of a change in tax rates on our deferred tax assets and liabilities is recognized as income or expense in the period that includes the enactment date.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (&#x201C;Tax Act&#x201D;) was enacted on December&nbsp;22, 2017 reducing the Company&#x2019;s &nbsp;federal corporate tax rate from 34% to 21%, effective January&nbsp;1, 2018. &nbsp;For deferred tax assets and liabilities, amounts were remeasured based on the applicable tax rate, which is now 21%. Based on this new law, we recorded an additional tax expense of $2.0 million due to the revaluation of the company&#x2019;s deferred tax asset in 2017. The Tax Act repealed the corporate Alternative Minimum Tax (&#x201C;AMT&#x201D;) and as a result a portion of the Company&#x2019;s AMT credit carryover from prior years will be refundable beginning in 2018.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Management Strategy</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our strategy is to operate as an independent, business- and retail- oriented financial institution dedicated to serving customers in our market area. &nbsp;Our commitment is to provide a broad range of products and services to meet the needs of our customers. &nbsp;As part of this commitment, we are looking to increase our emphasis on commercial business products and services. &nbsp;We also operate a fully interactive transactional website that also allows consumers to open accounts. &nbsp;In addition, we are continually looking at cost-effective ways to expand our market area. &nbsp;Financial highlights of our strategy have included:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Broadening Loan Portfolio Diversification. &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">We continue to work toward diversifying our loan portfolio to reduce our reliance on any one type of loan. &nbsp;Approximately 56.5% of our loan portfolio consisted of loans other than consumer real estate loans at the end of 2017. &nbsp;At the end of 2018, that&nbsp;percentage had increased to 63.7%, reflecting an increase of $282.7 million in our commercial and non-residential consumer loan portfolios.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Continuing as a Leading One-to-four family Lender in Indiana. &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">We are one of the largest originators of one-to-four family residential loans in our market area. &nbsp;During 2018, we originated $186.9 million of one-to-four family residential first mortgage loans. &nbsp;While the last economic downturn decreased real estate values, we have seen a stabilization in purchase activity in our market areas. Interest rates increasing slightly has also led to a slight decline in one-to-four family residential first mortgage loans originated in 2018.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">

		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Bank made significant progress in its strategy to increase commercial and consumer loans as we increased the commercial portfolio by $210.6 million and the non-residential consumer portfolio by $72.1 million during 2018 primarily due to the Universal acquisition and indirect lending growth. &nbsp;We actively seek out opportunities to provide financing for new and growing commercial borrowers, as well as refinancing to sound commercial borrowers currently served by other financial institutions. &nbsp;The increase in the commercial and consumer portfolios was offset by selling $122.3 million of consumer residential mortgage loans during the period and a decline in residential mortgage loan originations as rates are starting to slowly increase. &nbsp;The Bank continues to sell longer term fixed-rate mortgage loans to reduce related interest rate risk.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Delinquencies and Non-performing Assets</font><font style="display:inline;">. &nbsp;As of December&nbsp;31, 2018, our total loans delinquent 30&#8209;to&#8209;89&nbsp;days&nbsp;were&nbsp;$20.1 million, or 1.3% of total loans, compared to $15.6 million, or 1.3% of total loans, at the end of 2017.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">At December&nbsp;31, 2018, our non-performing assets totaled $11.1 million, or 0.54% of total assets, compared to $6.0 million, or 0.38% of total assets, at December&nbsp;31, 2017. &nbsp;This $5.1 million, or 85.8%,&nbsp;increase was due to an&nbsp;increase in non-performing&nbsp;loans primarily in the commercial real estate loan portfolio and other real estate owned acquired in the acquisition of Universal. &nbsp;The table below sets forth the amounts and categories of non-performing assets in our loan portfolio at the dates indicated.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;">Specific loan loss allocation related to loans that have been individually evaluated for impairment remained unchanged throughout the&nbsp;year, and general loan loss reserves have increased $894,000 as the non-performing loans and classified assets increased from 2017 to 2018, and the loan portfolio grew. &nbsp;Net charge-offs for the&nbsp;year 2018 were $1.2 million, or 0.09% of average loans on an annualized basis, compared to $1.2 million, or 0.10% of average loans, for 2017. &nbsp;As of December&nbsp;31, 2018, the allowance for loan losses as a&nbsp;percentage of loans receivable and non-performing loans was 0.89% and 145.9%, respectively, compared to 1.05% and 235.9%, respectively, at December&nbsp;31, 2017. &nbsp;Allowance for loan losses as a&nbsp;percentage of loans receivable decreased primarily due to an increase in the total loan portfolio. &nbsp;Allowance for loan losses as a&nbsp;percentage of non-performing loans decreased due to the increase in non-performing loans as of December&nbsp;31, 2018. &nbsp;The increase in the allowance was primarily due to management&#x2019;s ongoing evaluation of the loan portfolio conditions in our market areas.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Other Assets. &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">Other material changes in our assets during 2018 include an&nbsp;increase in premises and equipment, cash value of life insurance and goodwill of $4.1 million,&nbsp;$7.5 million and $20.5 million, respectively,&nbsp;as a result of the acquisition of Universal. &nbsp;Details regarding the acquisition are discussed in Note 2 of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements contained in Item 8 of this Form 10-K.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;"></font>

			<font style="display:inline;">The Company acquired $5.0 million of subordinated debentures in the 2008 acquisition of another financial institution. &nbsp;The net balance of these securities as of December&nbsp;31, 2018 was $4.2 million due to the purchase accounting adjustment made at the time of the acquisition. &nbsp;The securities bear the prevailing three-month LIBOR rate plus 170 basis points. &nbsp;The Company has the right to redeem the trust preferred securities, in whole or in part, without penalty. &nbsp;These securities mature on September&nbsp;15, 2035.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">The Company also acquired $5.0 million of subordinated debentures in the acquisition of Universal during 2018. The net balance of these securities as of December&nbsp;31, 2018 was $4.0 million due to the purchase accounting adjustment made at the time of the acquisition. &nbsp;The securities bear the&nbsp;prevailing three-month interest rate of LIBOR plus 169 basis points. &nbsp;The Company has the right to redeem the trust preferred securities, in whole or in part, without penalty. &nbsp;These securities mature on October 7, 2035.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company borrowed $10.0 million in two $5.0 million term notes from First Tennessee Bank, N.A. to use in the acquisition of Universal. These loans had a combined balance of $9.7 million at December 31, 2018. The fixed rate term note had a balance of $4.7 million and matures 5 years from the date of issuance, or February 28, 2023. This term note bears a fixed rate of interest of 4.99% per annum and requires quarterly principal payments, which began March 31, 2018. The variable rate term note matures 5 years from the date of issuance, or February 28, 2023. This term note bears a rate of interest of the prevailing three-month LIBOR rate plus 195 basis points, which was 4.35% at December 31, 2018. The Company has the right to redeem either note at any time, in whole or in part, without penalty.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Stockholders&#x2019; Equity</font><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">Stockholders&#x2019; equity was $202.4 million as of December&nbsp;31, 2018, an increase of $52.1 million from December&nbsp;31, 2017. The increase was primarily due to net income available to common shareholders of $18.9 million and the&nbsp;issuance of common stock related to the Universal acquisition of $42.3 million. &nbsp;These increases were partially offset by cash dividends of $6.4 million. &nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s tangible book value per common share as of December&nbsp;31, 2018 increased to $20.51 compared to $20.08 as of December&nbsp;31, 2017 and the tangible common equity ratio decreased to 8.72% as of December&nbsp;31, 2018 compared to 9.35% as of December&nbsp;31, 2017. &nbsp;The Bank&#x2019;s risk-based capital ratios were well in excess of &#x201C;well-capitalized&#x201D; levels as defined by all regulatory standards as of December&nbsp;31, 2018.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">Rate/Volume Analysis</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The following table presents the dollar amount of changes in interest income and interest expense for major components of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities. &nbsp;For each category of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities, information is provided on changes attributable to changes in volume, which are changes in volume multiplied by the old rate, and changes in rate, which is a change in rate multiplied by the old volume. &nbsp;Changes attributable to both rate and volume, which cannot be segregated, are allocated proportionately to the change due to volume and the change due to rate.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Comparison of Results of Operations for the&nbsp;Years Ended December&nbsp;31, 2018 and 2017.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">General</font><font style="display:inline;">. &nbsp;Net income available to common stockholders for the&nbsp;year ended December&nbsp;31, 2018 was $18.9 million, or $2.25 basic and $2.21 diluted earnings per common share, compared to net income available to common stockholders of $12.3 million, or $1.67 basic and $1.64 diluted earnings per common share, for the&nbsp;year ended December&nbsp;31, 2017. Net income&nbsp;for 2018 includes $1.9 million of one-time merger and system conversion expenses, net of tax, related to the acquisition of Universal. The details of our 2018 performance are set forth below and in our Consolidated Audited Financial Statements contained in Item&nbsp;8 of this Form&nbsp;10&#8209;K, &nbsp;and regarding the acquisition are discussed in Note 2.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Interest Income</font><font style="display:inline;">. &nbsp;Total interest income increased $20.8 million, or 35.4%, to $79.7 million during the&nbsp;year ended December&nbsp;31, 2018 from $58.9 million during the&nbsp;year ended December&nbsp;31, 2017. &nbsp;The increase was a result of the $342.4 million increase in average interest-earning assets to $1.8 billion at&nbsp;year end 2018&nbsp;and a forty&nbsp;basis point increase in yield on average interest-earning assets to 4.39% in 2018 compared to 3.99% in 2017, due to the Universal acquisition and organic loan growth. &nbsp;Interest income on loans in 2018 was $68.5 million compared to $51.2 million in 2017, a result of a $241.5 million increase in average loan balances and a forty-eight&nbsp;basis point increase in the weighted average yield on average loans in 2018 to 4.80%. &nbsp;Interest income on investments, including FHLB stock, increased in 2018 by $3.5 million to $11.0 million primarily due to the Universal acquisition.&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Interest Expense</font><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">Interest expense increased $6.0 million, or 56.4%, to $16.6 million during the&nbsp;year ended December&nbsp;31, 2018 compared to $10.6 million during the&nbsp;year ended December&nbsp;31, 2017. &nbsp;The reason for this increase was an increase in average interest-bearing liabilities of $251.9 million and a twenty-six&nbsp;basis point increase in weighted average rate paid on average interest-bearing liabilities. &nbsp;The </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:11.7647058823529%;margin-right:11.7647058823529%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">63</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:11.7647058823529%;margin-right:11.7647058823529%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:11.7647058823529%;margin-right:11.7647058823529%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#TOC"><font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:11.7647058823529%;margin-right:11.7647058823529%;"><p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;">increase in average interest-bearing liabilities was a result of a $211.6 million increase in average interest-bearing deposits, primarily due to the Universal acquisition and&nbsp;an increase of $40.3 million in average FHLB advances and other borrowings primarily as additional funding was used to fund increased loan demand and the Universal acquisition.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;color:#000000;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Net Interest Income</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">Net interest income before the provision for loan losses increased $14.8 million in 2018 compared to 2017. &nbsp;The increase was a result of an increase of $342.4 million in average interest earning assets due primarily to an increase in the average loan portfolio of $241.5 million. This increase was aided by the average net interest margin increasing to 3.47% in 2018 compared to 3.27% in 2017, while the average tax equivalent net interest margin increased to 3.55% in 2018 compared to 3.38% in 2017. &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;">For more information on our asset/liability management, especially as it relates to interest rate risk, see &#x201C;Item&nbsp;7A&nbsp;- Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk&#x201D; in this Form&nbsp;10&#8209;K.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Provision for Loan Losses</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">The provision for loan losses for 2018 was $2.1 million compared to $1.2 million during 2017. &nbsp;The increase was primarily a result of our organic loan portfolio growth over the last&nbsp;year and an increase in our non-performing assets. &nbsp;The loan mix also contributed to the increase in provision with commercial and non-real estate consumer loans making up 63.7% of the loan portfolio at the end of 2018 compared to 57.0% at of the end of 2017.&nbsp;Net charge-offs for 2018&nbsp;and 2017 remained consistent at&nbsp;$1.2 million, or 0.09% and 0.10% of total average loans, respectively.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-style:italic;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Non-Interest Income</font><font style="display:inline;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;font-style:normal;">Non-interest income increased by $1.5 million to $19.6 million in 2018.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">The increase in non-interest expenses was primarily due to&nbsp;an increase of $5.7 million in salaries and employee benefits expense and $2.2 million of other expenses, a majority of which&nbsp;was a result of the acquisition and integration of Universal. The number of full-time employees increased from 390 at year end 2017 to 485 at year end 2018 causing the increase in salaries and employee benefits.&nbsp;Other increases related to the acquisition and integration of Universal included&nbsp;an increase of $832,000 of net occupancy expenses with the addition of 12 financial centers, an increase in equipment expenses of $741,000, &nbsp;an increase of $614,000 on ATM and debit card expenses and a &nbsp;$517,000 increase in software subscription and maintenance expenses. &nbsp;Intangible amortization increased as a result of the amortization of the $4.5 million of the Universal purchase price allocated to a &nbsp;core deposit intangible. One-time pretax merger-related expenses were $2.4 million consisting primarily of merger-related salaries and employee benefits expenses, service and software contract cancellation expenses including deconversion and professional fees.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Income Tax Expense</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;">. &nbsp;Income tax expense in 2018&nbsp;decreased&nbsp;$3.8 million compared to 2017. &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">The effective tax rate for 2018 was 13.6% compared to 35.6% for 2017. &nbsp;The reason for the decrease was primarily due to additional tax expense in 2017 caused by the revaluation of the Company&#x2019;s deferred tax asset and the reduction in&nbsp;the Company&#x2019;s &nbsp;federal corporate tax rate to 21% effective January&nbsp;1, 2018,&nbsp;both a result of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act which was enacted into law in December&nbsp;2017. The effective tax rate excluding the $2.0 million tax expense resulting from the revaluation was 25.1% in 2017. &nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Interest Income</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;color:#000000;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Total interest income increased $5.1 million, or 9.4%, to $58.9 million during the year ended December 31, 2017 from $53.8 million during the year ended December 31, 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;The increase was a result of the $68.7 million increase in average interest-earning assets to $1.5 billion at year end 2017 and a sixteen basis point increase in yield on average interest-earning assets to 3.99% in 2017 compared to 3.83% in 2016 as average interest earning assets reprice higher.&nbsp;&nbsp;Interest income on loans in 2017 was $51.2 million compared to $46.8 million in 2016, a result of a $66.5 million increase in average loan balances and a fourteen basis point increase in the weighted average yield on average loans in 2017 to 4.32%.&nbsp;&nbsp;Interest income on investments, including FHLB stock, increased in 2017 by $566,000 to $7.5 million.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:27.5pt;color:#000000;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;color:#000000;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Interest Expense</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;">.</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;color:#000000;"> &nbsp;Interest expense increased $1.4 million, or 14.8%, to $10.6 million during the year ended December 31, 2017 compared to $9.2 million during the year ended December 31, 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;The reason for this increase was an increase in average interest-bearing liabilities of $42.2 million and a five basis point increase in the expense on average advances.&nbsp;&nbsp;The increase in average interest-bearing liabilities was a result of a $57.5 million increase in average interest-bearing deposits, as additional funding was used to fund increased loan demand, partially offset by a decrease of $15.3 million in average FHLB advances.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:27.5pt;color:#000000;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;color:#000000;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Net Interest Income</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;color:#000000;">.&nbsp; </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;">Net interest income before the provision for loan losses increased $3.7 million in 2017 compared to 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;The increase was a result of an increase of $68.6 million in average interest earning assets due to an increase in the average loan portfolio of $66.5 million. This increase was aided by the net interest margin increasing to 3.27% in 2017 compared to 3.17% in 2016, while the tax equivalent net interest margin increased to 3.38% in 2017 compared to 3.27% in 2016.&nbsp; </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;color:#000000;">For more information on our asset/liability management especially as it relates to interest rate risk, see &#x201C;Item 7A - Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk&#x201D; in this Form 10-K.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:27.5pt;color:#000000;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Provision for Loan Losses</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;color:#000000;">.&nbsp; </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;">The provision for loan losses for 2017 was $1.2 million compared to $850,000 during 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;The increase was primarily due to our loan portfolio that has increased $10.6 million, or 0.9% over the last year and a slightly increased level of net charge-offs.&nbsp;&nbsp;The loan mix also has contributed to the increase in provision with commercial and non-real estate consumer loans making up 57.0% of the loan portfolio at the end of 2017 compared to 53.2% as of the end of 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Net charge-offs for 2017 equaled $1.2 million, or 0.10% of total average loans compared to $1.1 million, or 0.10% of total average loans in 2016.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;color:#000000;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;color:#000000;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Non-Interest Income</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;color:#000000;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Non-interest income decreased by $1.3 million to $18.1 million in 2017.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
