</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#TOC"><font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Items Measured at Fair Value on a Recurring Basis</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Following is a description of the valuation methodologies and inputs used for instruments measured at fair value on a recurring basis and recognized in the accompanying comparative balance sheet, as well as the general classification of such instruments pursuant to the valuation hierarchy.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-decoration:underline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-style:italic;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Available for Sale Securities</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Where quoted market prices are available in an active market, securities are classified within Level&nbsp;1 of the valuation hierarchy. &nbsp;The Company uses a third-party provider to provide market prices on its securities. &nbsp;Pooled trust preferred securities prices are evaluated by a third party. &nbsp;Level 1 securities include marketable equity securities. &nbsp;If quoted market prices are not available, then fair values are estimated by using pricing models, quoted prices of securities with similar characteristics or discounted cash flows. &nbsp;Level&nbsp;2 securities include mortgage-backed, collateralized mortgage obligations, municipal, federal agency and certain corporate obligation securities. &nbsp;In certain cases where Level 1 or Level&nbsp;2 inputs are not available, securities are classified within Level 3 of the hierarchy and include certain corporate obligation securities.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Third party vendors compile prices from various sources and may apply such techniques as matrix pricing to determine the value of identical or similar investment securities (Level 2). &nbsp;Matrix pricing is a mathematical technique widely used in the banking industry to value investment securities without relying exclusively on quoted prices for specific investment securities but rather relying on investment securities relationship to other benchmark quoted investment securities. &nbsp;Any investment security not valued based upon the methods above are considered Level 3.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-decoration:underline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-style:italic;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Interest Rate Derivative Agreements</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Interest rate swap positions, both assets and liabilities, are valued by a third-party pricing agent using an income approach and utilizing models that use as their basis readily observable market parameters. This valuation process considers various factors including interest rate yield curves, time value and volatility factors.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The following table presents the fair value measurements of assets and liabilities measured on a recurring basis and the level within the ASC 820 fair value hierarchy.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Item&nbsp;9.&nbsp;&nbsp;Changes In and Disagreements With Accountants on Accounting and Financial Disclosure<a name="Item9ChangesInandDisagreementsWithAccoun"></a></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">None.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Item&nbsp;9A.&nbsp;&nbsp;Controls and Procedures<a name="Item9AControlsandProcedures_836060"></a></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;color:#000000;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We maintain a system of disclosure controls and procedures </font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;">(as defined in SEC Rule&nbsp;13a&#8209;15(e)&nbsp;of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the &#x201C;Exchange Act&#x201D;)) </font><font style="display:inline;">that is designed to provide reasonable assurance that information required to be disclosed by us in the reports that we file under the Exchange Act is recorded, processed, summarized and reported accurately and within the time periods specified in the SEC&#x2019;s &nbsp;rules&nbsp;and forms, and that such information is accumulated and communicated to our management, including our principal executive officer and principal financial officer, as appropriate. &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;">An evaluation of the Company&#x2019;s disclosure controls and procedures as of December&nbsp;31, 2018, was carried out under the supervision and with the participation of our Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer and several other members of our senior management preceding the filing date of this annual report. &nbsp;Our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer concluded that, as of December&nbsp;31, 2018, the Company&#x2019;s disclosure controls and procedures were effective in ensuring that the information required to be disclosed by the Company in the reports it files or submits under the Exchange Act is (i)&nbsp;accumulated and communicated to the Company&#x2019;s management (including our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer) in a timely manner, and (ii)&nbsp;recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in the SEC&#x2019;s &nbsp;rules&nbsp;and forms.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company does not expect that its disclosure controls and procedures will prevent all error and all fraud. &nbsp;A control procedure, no matter how well conceived and operated, can provide only reasonable, not absolute, assurance that the objectives of the control procedure are met. &nbsp;Because of the inherent limitations in all control procedures, no evaluation of controls can provide absolute assurance that all control issues and instances of fraud, if any, within MutualFirst have been detected. &nbsp;These inherent limitations include the realities that judgment in decision-making can be faulty, and that breakdowns can occur because of simple error or mistake. &nbsp;Additionally, controls can be circumvented by the individual acts of some persons, by collusion of two or more people, or by management override of the control. &nbsp;The design of any control procedure also is based in part upon certain assumptions about the likelihood of future events, and there can be no assurance that any design will succeed in achieving its stated goals under all potential future conditions; over time, controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate. &nbsp;Because of the inherent limitations in a cost-effective control procedure, misstatements due to error or fraud may occur and not be detected.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Management&#x2019;s Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The management of MutualFirst Financial,&nbsp;Inc. is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting. &nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance to the Company&#x2019;s management and board of directors regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of the financial statements for external purposes in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that (i)&nbsp;pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the Company; (ii)&nbsp;provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America, and that receipts and expenditures of the Company are being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the Company; and (iii)&nbsp;provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use, or disposition of the Company&#x2019;s assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">126</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#TOC"><font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Because of its inherent limitations, internal controls over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements. All internal control systems, no matter how well designed, have inherent limitations, including the possibility of human error and the circumvention of overriding controls. &nbsp;Accordingly, even effective internal control over financial reporting can provide only reasonable assurance with respect to financial statement preparation. &nbsp;Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our management assessed the effectiveness of the Company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting as of December&nbsp;31, 2018. In making this assessment, it used the criteria set forth by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO) in</font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;"> Internal Control-Integrated Framework (2013)</font><font style="display:inline;">. &nbsp;As permitted by SEC guidance, management excluded from its assessment the operations of the Universal Bancorp acquisition made during 2018, which are described in Note 2: Acquisitions, included within the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements in Item 8 of this Form 10-K. The total assets of the entity acquired in this acquisition represented approximately 12% of the Company&#x2019;s consolidated assets as of December 31, 2018. Based on our assessment, we believe that, as of December&nbsp;31, 2018, the Company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting was effective based on the specified criteria.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:center;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;">Audit Committee, Board of Directors and Stockholders</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;">MutualFirst Financial,&nbsp;Inc.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;">Muncie, Indiana</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Opinion on the Internal Control over Financial Reporting</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">We have audited MutualFirst Financial, Inc.'s (the "Company") internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2018, based on criteria established in </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:normal;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Internal Control &#x2013; Integrated Framework:&nbsp;&nbsp;(2013)</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;"> issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO). </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">In our opinion, the Company maintained, in all material respects, effective internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2018, based on criteria established in </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:normal;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Internal Control &#x2013; Integrated Framework:&nbsp;&nbsp;(2013)</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;"> issued by COSO. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;">As described in Management&#x2019;s Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting, management excluded from its assessment the internal control over financial reporting related to Universal Bancorp., which was acquired on February 28, 2019 and whose assets constitute approximately 12% of total assets of the consolidated financial statement amounts as of and for the year ended December 31, 2018. Accordingly, our audit did not include the internal control over financial reporting related to Universal Bancorp.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">We also have audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States) ("PCAOB"), the consolidated financial statements of the Company and our report dated March 15, 2019, expressed an unqualified opinion thereon.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Basis for Opinion</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">The Company's management is responsible for maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting and for its assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting, included in the accompanying Management&#x2019;s Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Company's internal control over financial reporting based on our audit.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">We are a public accounting firm registered with the PCAOB and are required to be independent with respect to the Company in accordance with the U.S. federal securities laws and the applicable rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission and the PCAOB.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">We conducted our audit in accordance with the standards of the PCAOB.&nbsp;&nbsp;Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether effective internal control over financial reporting was maintained in all material respects.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">Our audit included obtaining an understanding of internal control over financial reporting, assessing the risk that a material weakness exists and testing and evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of internal control based on the assessed risk.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our audit also included performing such other procedures as we considered necessary in the circumstances.&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe that our audit provides a reasonable basis for our opinion.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Definitions and Limitations of Internal Control over Financial Reporting</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">A company's internal control over financial reporting is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.&nbsp;&nbsp;A company's internal control over financial </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">128</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#TOC"><font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">reporting includes those policies and procedures that (1) pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company; (2) provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company are being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the company; and (3) provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use or disposition of the company's assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements.&nbsp;&nbsp;Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 12pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 12pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">/s/ BKD, </font><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:8pt;">LLP</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Indianapolis, Indiana</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">March&nbsp;15, 2019</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;"></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Changes in Internal Controls over Financial Reporting</font>
